subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should OpenClaw mobile apps support arbitrary per-gateway custom headers, or should native proxy authentication be limited to narrower typed schemes such as Basic/Bearer first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent boundary controls pre-Gateway credentials, native secure storage, diagnostics redaction, TLS requirements, and whether arbitrary operator-supplied headers are safe for mobile clients.

options.title: Approve typed static proxy auth first
options.body: Support a staged Basic/Bearer/fixed-header contract with secure storage, TLS gating, redaction, gateway-only attachment, and platform parity before considering arbitrary custom headers.

options.title: Approve arbitrary custom headers
options.body: Allow general name/value header pairs per gateway, accepting a broader security and UX review surface for validation, redaction, and forbidden-header rules.

options.title: Defer native proxy credentials
options.body: Keep mobile reverse-proxy header injection unsupported for now and document Tailscale, VPN, or proxy-bypass alternatives while the broader design remains unsettled.

recommendation.title: Approve typed static proxy auth first
recommendation.body: Support a staged Basic/Bearer/fixed-header contract with secure storage, TLS gating, redaction, gateway-only attachment, and platform parity before considering arbitrary custom headers.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the issue author and has the strongest current signal across the security/product boundary and recent mobile gateway connection history.
